audits.title: Clinical outcome assessment in mammography: an audit of 7,506 screening and diagnostic mammography examinations.

cycle1.result: Recall rate 10.9%; screening sensitivity 100% and specificity 88%; screening cancer detection rate 6.1 per thousand; screening PPV1 4.9%.

audits.other_findings: Diagnostic group had higher PPV and more advanced cancers than benchmarks, needing further audit.
audits.citation: Tunçbilek I, Ozdemir A, Gültekin S, Oğur T, Erman R, Yüce C. Clinical outcome assessment in mammography: an audit of 7,506 screening and diagnostic mammography examinations. Diagn Interv Radiol. 2007;13(4):183-187. PMID: 18092288.

audits.title: Adjusting mammography--audit recommendations in a lower-incidence Taiwanese population.
audits.standard: ACR BI-RADS medical audit recommendations, with adjusted targets for Taiwan (PPV1 1.7%-3.4%; cancer detection 0.7-3.4 per 1,000)
audits.setting: Hospital-based breast imaging department, Chi-Mei Medical Center, Tainan

cycle1.result: 89 biopsies, 22 cancers; PPV1 3.1%, PPV2 16.2%, PPV3 24.7%; cancer detection 2.7 per 1,000; minimal cancer 50%; node-negative 71.4%; recall rate 8.5%.

audits.other_findings: Results fitted the proposed population-adjusted BI-RADS benchmarks.
audits.citation: Chen CY, Tzeng WS, Tsai CC, Mak CW, Chen CH, Chou MC. Adjusting mammography--audit recommendations in a lower-incidence Taiwanese population. J Am Coll Radiol. 2008;5(9):978-985. doi:10.1016/j.jacr.2008.05.009. PMID: 18755438.

audits.title: [Outcome of a screening mammography practice with regard to epidemiological audit].
audits.setting: Breast diagnostic clinic, CDE Diagnostico por Imagem, Campinas

cycle1.result: Screening detection rate 0.34%; biopsy recommended in 1.7%; recall rate 19%; PPV1 1.65%; PPV2 21.9%; 28% minimal carcinomas.

audits.other_findings: Detection and minimal/in situ rates comparable to established values but PPV lower than ideal.
audits.citation: Camargo Júnior HS, Camargo MM, Teixeira SR, Arruda Mde S, Azevedo J. [Outcome of a screening mammography practice with regard to epidemiological audit]. Rev Bras Ginecol Obstet. 2009;31(10):508-512. doi:10.1590/s0100-72032009001000007. PMID: 19942999.

audits.title: Medical audit of a rapid-throughput mammography screening practice: methodology and results of 27,114 examinations.
audits.standard: Medical audit of screening mammography performance measures
audits.setting: Rapid-throughput mammography screening practice, University of California, San Francisco

cycle1.result: Sensitivity 93.1%, specificity 94.2%, positive predictive value 10.0%; biopsy malignancy yield 32.1%; 170 cancers, 76.5% stage 0 or 1.

audits.other_findings: Median cancer size 12 mm; axillary nodal metastasis 11.0%.
audits.citation: Sickles EA, Ominsky SH, Sollitto RA, Galvin HB, Monticciolo DL. Medical audit of a rapid-throughput mammography screening practice: methodology and results of 27,114 examinations. Radiology. 1990;175(2):323-327. doi:10.1148/radiology.175.2.2326455. PMID: 2326455.

audits.title: Complete internal audit of a mammography service in a reference institution for breast imaging.
audits.standard: BI-RADS recommended complete audit and literature benchmarks
audits.setting: Private reference institution for breast imaging (FEMME), São Paulo

cycle1.result: Cancer detection 4.8 per 1,000 mammograms; PPV for BI-RADS 3, 4 and 5 were 1.3%, 41.3% and 100%; sensitivity 97.1%, specificity 97.4%.

audits.other_findings: Of 7,249 screening mammograms, 1.43% were category 0 and 80.76% category 2; DCIS formed 22.8% of cancers.
audits.citation: Badan GM, Roveda Júnior D, Ferreira CA, de Noronha Junior OA. Complete internal audit of a mammography service in a reference institution for breast imaging. Radiol Bras. 2014;47(2):74-78. doi:10.1590/s0100-39842014000200007. PMID: 25741052.

audits.title: Value of audits in breast cancer screening quality assurance programmes.
audits.standard: Screening outcome indicators (recall rate, detection rate, sensitivity) with radiological review
audits.setting: All 17 reading units of the Dutch breast cancer screening programme; triennial audits by the Dutch Reference Centre for Screening

cycle1.result: Recall rate 0.66%, detection rate 3.3 per 1000, sensitivity 64.5%.

audits.intervention: Repeated triennial audits with radiological review and feedback

cycle2.result: Recall rate 1.58%, detection rate 5.4 per 1000, sensitivity 71.6%.

audits.other_findings: Four audit series in total; proportion of missed cancers did not change (p = 0.4).
audits.citation: Geertse TD, Holland R, Timmers JM, Paap E, Pijnappel RM, Broeders MJ, et al.. Value of audits in breast cancer screening quality assurance programmes. Eur Radiol. 2015;25(11):3338-3347. doi:10.1007/s00330-015-3744-x. PMID: 25903711.

audits.title: [An audit of breast cancer screening mammograms and the variability of radiological practice].
audits.setting: Radiology, Hospital San Juan de Dios del Aljarafe, Seville (general hospital)

cycle1.result: Recall 9.48% (16.1% initial, 8.2% revisions); PPV1 6.52%, PPV2 55%; sensitivity 100%, specificity 91%; cancer detection 6.1/1000

audits.other_findings: Results within reference values except recall rate, which varied significantly by radiologist (12% and 17.2% vs 7.3%).
audits.citation: Moreno-Ramos MD, Ruíz-García E. [An audit of breast cancer screening mammograms and the variability of radiological practice]. Rev Calid Asist. 2016;31(3):146-151. doi:10.1016/j.cali.2015.09.002. PMID: 26597028.

audits.title: Trends in Attaining Mammography Quality Benchmarks With Repeated Participation in a Quality Measurement Program: Going Beyond the Mammography Quality Standards Act to Address Breast Cancer Disparities.
audits.standard: 13 mammography quality measures and benchmarks (tracking, callback, cancer detection, loss to follow-up, timeliness)

cycle1.result: Baseline benchmark attainment (figures not reported in abstract).

audits.intervention: Repeated participation in a quality measurement programme with benchmark reporting.

cycle2.result: Number of facilities meeting benchmarks increased with length of participation for many measures, including cancer detection, timely imaging and not lost at biopsy.

audits.citation: Rauscher GH, Tossas-Milligan K, Macarol T, Grabler PM, Murphy AM. audits.title: Sustaining Mammography Image Quality With a Technologist Coaching Program in the Era of the Enhancing Quality Using the Inspection Program (EQUIP).
audits.standard: Overall mammogram quality passing criteria; QI goal of 90% (EQUIP era)
audits.setting: Breast imaging service (University of Utah and Stanford authors)

cycle1.result: 74% (1098/1489) of audited mammograms met overall passing criteria.

audits.intervention: Long-term technologist coaching programme started September 2015, after an earlier QI initiative.

cycle2.result: 90% (8902/9929) of audited mammograms met overall passing criteria.

audits.other_findings: Post-improvement period (February to August 2015) pass rate was 93% (501/541); both later periods were significantly higher than the improvement period.
audits.citation: Kozlov A, Larson D, DeMartini WB, Pal S, Cowart P, Strain A, et al.. Sustaining Mammography Image Quality With a Technologist Coaching Program in the Era of the Enhancing Quality Using the Inspection Program (EQUIP). J Breast Imaging. 2023;5(6):675-684. doi:10.1093/jbi/wbad075. PMID: 38141238.

audits.title: A private breast imaging practice: medical audit of 25,788 screening and 1,077 diagnostic examinations.
audits.setting: Private breast imaging practice, St Luke's Regional Medical Center, Boise

cycle1.result: Screening recall 5.9%; sensitivity 91%; positive predictive value 11%; 119 of 188 (63%) cancers stage 0 or 1.

audits.other_findings: Diagnostic examinations: sensitivity 97%, PPV 24%, 27% referred for biopsy.
